topic.title: How a Crossrail tunnel boring machine dug the Elizabeth line under London, lining the tunnel as it went, and passed a working Tube line

title: How Did Crossrail Tunnel Past the Tube?
description:
How did Crossrail dig a new railway through ground already full of Tube tunnels?
We walk a 150-metre tunnel boring machine from its spinning cutterhead to the arm that builds the tunnel's concrete rings behind it, then show how close it came to the Northern line.
Sources: Arup (Nov 2026).
Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.
cta: Which machine should we take apart next? Comment

lines.text: Crossrail dug a railway between London's Tube tunnels.
How? Its machines were 150 metres long, and each built the tunnel as it dug.
At the front, a steel wheel spins into the clay, cutting a hole 7.1 metres across.
Why doesn't the ground cave in? Dug clay fills a sealed chamber that pushes back.
Where does it go? A conveyor carries the clay back along the machine.
At the back, an arm bolts concrete pieces into a ring, lining the tunnel.
It pushes off each ring and creeps forward. Together, the machines dug 42 kilometres under London.
Over 17,000 buildings, rails and pipes were checked for movement. At Tottenham Court Road, the Northern line was already there.
The new tunnel passed over it with just 700 millimetres to spare.
A new line, threaded between the old ones.

Beat 'ring': 'an arm bolts curved concrete pieces into a ring, a tunnel 7.1 metres across' with the diameter bracket spanning the ring is wrong. 7.1 m is the excavated (cutterhead) diameter; the concrete ring is 6.8 m outside and 6.2 m inside (Crossrail Learning Legacy, Machine-driven tunnels on the Elizabeth line; Arup's '7.1m diameter tunnels' means the bored size). Fix: tie {fact3} to the hole the wheel cuts (e.g. 'the wheel cuts a hole 7.1 metres across', bracket on the cutterhead/bore in the wheel beat) or source the 6.2 m internal figure.

Beat 'forward': 'It pushes off each new ring and creeps forward, for 42 kilometres under central London' says one machine dug 42 km. Arup's 42 km is all the new tunnels together, dug by eight TBMs (about 26 miles total). Fix: e.g. 'Together, the machines dug 42 kilometres of tunnel under central London.'

Confirmed on the Arup page (WebFetch): 150 m long TBMs, 42 km of new tunnels, '7.1m diameter tunnels', 700 mm between the Elizabeth and Northern line tunnels at Tottenham Court Road, impact assessments on over 17,000 buildings, railways, major utilities and other assets. Description ends with the disclaimer. Note for the redo: Arup says the tunnels were threaded OVER the Northern line, so the 'checked'/'payoff' pictures should put the new tunnel above it, not level beside it.
